headlines.summary: PayPal is returning lots of cash to shareholders, but there could be an even bigger catalyst on the horizon.

headlines.title: PayPal Is Yesterday's News. Is This Fintech Stock the Better Buy?
headlines.summary: The digital payments enterprise is cheap, but it continues to operate from a position of fundamental weakness.

headlines.title: PayPal Holdings (PYPL) Pushes Deeper Into Credit And AI, Is It Still Undervalued?
headlines.summary: Recent moves at PayPal Holdings (PYPL) center on a bigger push into credit, Buy Now Pay Later and AI-driven payment infrastructure, alongside planned share buybacks and efforts to steady its checkout business. Recent buying interest around PayPal Holdings reflects this shift. The 90 day share price return of 18.78% contrasts with a year to date share price decline of 5.37% and a 1 year total shareholder return that has fallen 26.56%.

headlines.title: What You Need to Know Ahead of PayPal Holdings' Earnings Release
headlines.summary: PayPal Holdings will release its third-quarter earnings later this month, and analysts anticipate a low single-digit profit dip.

headlines.title: Has PayPal Stock Become A Different Bet?
headlines.summary: PayPal (PYPL) stock is priced at 9.8 times earnings. That compares with a multiple of 21.5 for the broader S&P 500. Investors looking at that price need a clear picture of the underlying business. The company, meanwhile, has shifted its priorities. During earlier earnings calls, executives highlighted branded checkout, the PayPal option shoppers select when paying online. Checkout is no longer the headline. So what does PayPal's management lead with now.

description: PayPal Holdings, Inc. operates a technology platform that enables digital payments for merchants and consumers worldwide. The company operates a two-sided network at scale that connects merchants and consumers that enables its customers to connect, transact, and send and receive payments through online and in person, as well as transfer and withdraw funds using various funding sources, such as bank accounts, PayPal or Venmo account balance, consumer credit and debit products, credit and debit cards, and cryptocurrencies, as well as other stored value products, including gift cards and eligible rewards. It provides payment solutions under the PayPal, PayPal Credit, Braintree, Venmo, Xoom, Hyperwallet, Honey, and Paidy names. The company was founded in 1998 and is headquartered in San Jose, California.
